notes: Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari chassis with Ferrari engines throughout. Private Ferraris of the 1950s share the works and engine and count as works under this rule.
Alfa Corse: Alfa Romeo's own team and engines.
Alfa Romeo works chassis with Alfa Romeo engines (Autodelta 1979-82; Euroracing 1983-85).
Talbot-Lago chassis and engines.
Officine Alfieri Maserati: Maserati chassis and engines. Private Maseratis share the works and engine and count as works under this rule.
English Racing Automobiles: own chassis and engines.
Alta: own chassis and engines (Geoffrey Taylor).
Amédée Gordini's team (Simca-Gordini): own chassis and engines.
Gordini: own chassis and engines.
OSCA (Maserati brothers): own chassis and engines.
British Racing Motors: own chassis and engines.
Veritas: own chassis and engines.
EMW (Eisenacher Motorenwerk): own chassis and engine.
Daimler-Benz's works team with its own straight-8.
Lancia: own chassis (D50) and engines.
Vanwall: own chassis and engines (Tony Vandervell).
Bugatti Type 251: own chassis and engine.
Porsche: own chassis and engines.
ATS (Automobili Turismo e Sport): own chassis and engine.
Honda's 1960s works team with its own engines.
Matra Sports: own chassis with the Matra V12 (1968 and 1970-72; 1969 Matra-Ford ran under Tyrrell).
Tecno: own chassis and flat-12.
Renault Sport works team with Renault engines.
Zakspeed: own chassis and turbo engines (Yamaha engines in 1989).

Renault owned the Enstone team from March 2000 (Benetton-Playlife 2000 and Benetton-Renault 2001 count as works) until Genii's majority purchase for 2010. 2010-15 (Genii; Lotus F1) is a customer under this rule though Renault stayed the engine partner.
Renault bought the team back for 2016 (Renault 2016-20; Alpine 2021-25).
Toyota Racing: own chassis and engines.
Honda Racing F1 (Brackley) after Honda's full purchase of BAR. BAR-Honda before 2006 (Honda 45% from late 2004) is a customer under this rule.
BMW Sauber: BMW owned the Hinwil team.
Mercedes-AMG Petronas: Mercedes owned the Brackley team (Brixworth engines). McLaren-Mercedes (Mercedes held 40% of the McLaren Group 2000-09) is a customer under this rule.
